cohort: Pregnant women in British Columbia who had a live birth or stillbirth at or after 20 weeks of gestation between 2004 and 2016
finding: Maternal anemia in pregnancy was associated with increased risks of various adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, including longer hospitalization, more antenatal admissions, preeclampsia, placenta previa, cesarean delivery, blood transfusion, preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, low Apgar score, and neonatal and perinatal death.
